grading_method.policy: grading-policy.md, applied to each current answer/evidence object independently
grading_method.scope: 2016 base/core multiplayer; all 63 literal frozen questions and unchanged expected answers
grading_method.procedure: Read every current reader-b object, frozen summary, fixed questions/key and supplied authoritative source text. Checked PDF p.19 structure-bonus tile images and p.29 popularity payout image. Compared requested material parts separately; did not consult other readers, previous grades, audits, parent history, web or other game evidence.
grading_method.local_evidence: Preserved each original answer, support label and evidence string. Evidence quotations or substantive statements can resolve parts; a bare section citation does not automatically supply an omitted requested condition. No cross-answer borrowing.
grading_method.equivalence_and_scope: Accept natural entailment and unambiguous shorthand for summary-defined operations. Do not require unasked key extras, repeated consequences of invoked operations, a full faction-exception inventory for normal rules, or numeric costs where the exposed-cost method determines them. Explain borderline decisions in per-answer reasons.

grade_rules.correct: All requested material parts resolved, no material contradiction or unsupported guess.
grade_rules.partial: Material requested omission/unresolved part without contradiction, including abstention.

grading_method.unsupported_guess: True only for a source-correct substantive claim absent from the frozen summary; mere reader support labels are not grades. None identified.

grades.question: How are Factory cards, encounter tokens, and the structure bonus set up, and who starts?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Select players + 1 Factory cards face-down and return others unseen; put tokens on 11 marked territories; randomly select one structure bonus tile face-up below Popularity Track. Lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

requested_parts.reason: The answer gives players + 1, face-down selection and unseen return, but does not state shuffling or random selection. Merely naming Setup step 1 in evidence locates the rule without stating the missing randomization.
Tokens are placed on the 11 marked territories.
One randomly selected face-up tile goes below the Popularity Track.
Lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

grades.reason: Partial: the requested Factory setup method omits shuffling/randomization required by PDF p. 6 and summary Setup step 1. Face-down selection establishes secrecy, but does not itself specify randomization. Clockwise subsequent play is unasked by "who starts" and is not separately required.

grades.question: What starts on the map and each mat, and which mat supplies starting power, combat cards, popularity, coins and objectives?
grades.expected_answer: Character on own home base; one worker on each of two land-adjoined territories. Faction Mat supplies power/combat cards, holds four mechs and six stars. Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.
grades.observed_answer: Character starts at home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; four mechs on Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six tech cubes in marked green boxes; structures/recruits in matching Player Mat spaces; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token ready beside mat. Faction Mat sets power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins and two objectives.

requested_parts.reason: Character at home and two workers on the two land-adjoined territories naturally means one worker on each, consistent with the setup table.
Four mechs cover abilities and six stars sit by the faction emblem.

Six cubes in marked green boxes, structures/recruits in their matching spaces, six workers on Produce and the token beside the mat identify the setup placements. "Marked green boxes" unambiguously identifies the black-square boxes in the supplied table; the answer need not redescribe the mark.
Faction Mat gives power/combat cards; Player Mat gives popularity, coins and two objectives.

grades.reason: Correct. The wording gives the piece placements and mat split. "Structures/recruits in matching Player Mat spaces" is unambiguous setup shorthand for placing those sets, rather than an unresolved placement choice; PDF pp. 7–9 and the summary setup table define those spaces.

grades.question: May you skip both actions, repeat a section, use top-row gains below, or take the bottom action first? How are costs and benefits determined?
grades.expected_answer: Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.
grades.observed_answer: You may take either, both, or neither action, but must move token to a different section; Rusviet may repeat a section, otherwise not. Top gains can pay bottom cost; bottom first is forbidden. Pay all exposed red costs first; choose as much or little green benefit as desired. Mat/upgrades determine exact costs/benefits.

requested_parts.reason: Either, both or neither is expressly allowed, with token movement required.
A different section is required except Rusviet.
Top gains can pay the bottom cost.
Bottom first is expressly forbidden.
All exposed red costs are paid first; as much or little green benefit as desired is available, with mat/upgrades determining amounts.

grades.question: Who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker, who can use the structure, and from where may you spend resources for an action elsewhere?
grades.expected_answer: Enemy worker controls territory and resources; structure owner retains abilities except cannot Produce at an uncontrolled Mill; enemy gains no structure ability. Spend resources from any controlled territories for actions anywhere; spent resources go to supply.
grades.observed_answer: An enemy worker on your structure territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure abilities; you retain those abilities even without control, except Mill cannot produce if uncontrolled. Spend resources from any territories you currently control, even for an action elsewhere.

requested_parts.reason: Worker controls territory and its resources.
Enemy cannot use it; owner retains ability except uncontrolled Mill cannot produce.
Any currently controlled territories can fund an action elsewhere.

grades.reason: Correct. All requested control/use/spending questions are answered. The key’s spent-token supply destination is useful context, but this question asks from where resources may be spent, not where spent tokens go (PDF pp. 4, 18).

grades.question: On a normal unupgraded Move, can one unit move twice, can a transported worker subsequently move, and who can carry what?
grades.expected_answer: Move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, sequentially, or gain $1 instead. All units carry any number of resources; only mechs carry any number of own workers, not characters. Carriage is not the worker movement so worker can subsequently move itself.
grades.observed_answer: No: normal Move selects up to two different units, one adjacent territory each. A carried worker may subsequently move itself. All units may carry any number of resources; only mechs may carry your workers, never your character.

requested_parts.reason: Two different units, one adjacent territory each, excludes using both selections on one unit.
A carried worker may subsequently move itself.
All units carry unlimited resources; only mechs carry own workers, never the character.

grades.reason: Correct. The $1 alternative and sequential resolution in the key are not additional requested parts of this movement/carry question. The stated restrictions match PDF pp. 5, 11.

Workers cannot enter independently while enemy workers control it.

grades.reason: Correct. "Even if at zero (loss cannot prevent retreat)" is naturally the zero-popularity retreat rule, not a competing claim permitting a negative track value; summary Move and PDF p. 11 expressly give that rule.

Attacker chooses.

Attacker wins.

grades.question: What presence establishes control of a territory, and do resources alone preserve your control after your last unit leaves a territory where you have no structure?
grades.expected_answer: You control a territory with at least one of your units, or with your structure and no enemy units. Resources are not units and do not establish control. If your last unit leaves and you have no structure there, you no longer control that territory or the resources left there; those resources cannot be spent by you unless you regain control.

Rulebook PDF p4, RESOURCES: resource tokens remain on the board and may be spent only from territories currently controlled.
Rulebook PDF p29, EVERY TERRITORY CONTROLLED and EVERY 2 RESOURCES CONTROLLED; PDF p31, END-GAME SCORING.
grades.observed_answer: Control is a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not preserve control after last unit leaves and no structure.
